overview: The Electric Mobility Promotion Scheme 2024 (EMPS-2024) was a subscheme under the PM Electric Drive Revolution in Innovative Vehicle Enhancement (PM E-DRIVE) Scheme, implemented from 1st April 2024 to 30th September 2024, aimed at promoting electric mobility through demand incentives for electric two-wheelers (e-2W) and three-wheelers (e-3W). It provided financial support based on battery capacity, with incentives of ₹5,000 per kWh for vehicles registered in FY 2024-25, subject to a cap of 15% of the ex-factory price. The scheme has been subsumed into the PM E-DRIVE Scheme, which runs from 1st October 2024 to 31st March 2026 with a total outlay of ₹10,900 crore.
objectives: Development of EV manufacturing eco-system in the country
eligibility: Eligible beneficiaries for e-2W and e-3W include individuals purchasing privately or corporate-owned registered electric two-wheelers and three-wheelers. Vehicles must be manufactured and registered within the validity period of EMPS-2024/PM E-DRIVE certificate. For e-ambulances, eligibility is decided in consultation with the Ministry of Health and Family Welfare. Incentives are not extended when EVs are purchased by Central or State Government departments or their agencies, as it constitutes passing funds between government heads.
benefits: Financial support in the form of upfront reduced purchase price for end-users, reimbursed to OEMs by the Ministry of Heavy Industries. Incentive rate: ₹5,000 per kWh for e-2W/e-3W registered in FY 2024-25, and ₹2,500 per kWh for those registered in FY 2025-26 under PM E-DRIVE. The incentive is capped at 15% of the ex-factory price, whichever is lower. Additional benefits include mandatory warranty requirements: 3 years or 20,000 km for e-2W, 3 years or 40,000 km for e-3W (e-rickshaw), and 3 years or 80,000 km for e-3W (L5).
financial_support: Demand incentives are provided at ₹5,000 per kWh for e-2W/e-3W registered in FY 2024-25 and ₹2,500 per kWh for FY 2025-26, subject to a cap of 15% of the ex-factory price. The incentive is reimbursed to OEMs after submission of claims. For e-buses, the incentive is ₹10,000 per kWh with size-based caps: standard bus (>10m & <=12m) up to ₹35,00,000, midi bus (>8m & <=10m) up to ₹25,00,000, and mini bus (>6m & <=8m) up to ₹20,00,000. Support for e-buses is released in four installments: 20% after supply order, 30% after commencement of commercial operation, 25% after 6 months, and 25% after 18 months of successful operation.
grant_amount_per_entity: 15% of ex-factory price or ₹5,000 per kWh (whichever is lower) for e-2W/e-3W; for e-buses: up to ₹35,00,000 for standard bus, ₹25,00,000 for midi bus, ₹20,00,000 for mini bus
application_process: 1. OEMs must apply for registration with the Ministry of Heavy Industries (MHI) by submitting Annexure-I (Manufacturer Registration Form) along with required documents including Company Registration Certificate, GST Registration, PAN Card, Testing/Homologation Certificate, Pre-registration of EV model, MOA/AOA, sales/service network proof, and photographs of the vehicle. 2. Submit hard copy of the application to Deputy Secretary (E-Mobility), Udyog Bhavan, New Delhi-110011. 3. MHI processes the application and confirms registration if found in order. 4. OEMs upload production data of EVs for which they seek incentives. 5. After sale, OEMs submit reimbursement claims within 120 days, accompanied by an undertaking (Annexure-III), board resolution (Annexure-IV), and photo ID proof. 6. Claims are verified by MHI and reimbursed upon validation.
required_documents: Application for manufacturer registration in Annexure-I
Testing/Homologation Certificate complying with PM E-DRIVE eligibility criteria
Pre-registration of EV model as per Annexure-II
Complete set of memorandum of association (MOA) and articles of association (AOA)
Proof of OEM’s sales and service network (list of at least 25 dealers/service centers in two states, or one service station for online sales)
Photographs of the type approved Vehicle
deadlines: The scheme was implemented from 1st April 2024 to 30th September 2024 and has been subsumed under PM E-DRIVE, which runs from 1st October 2024 to 31st March 2026.
caveats: Incentive is not extended when EVs are purchased by Central or State Government departments or agencies
Each individual beneficiary can avail incentive for not more than one EV of a particular category
All EV models must submit revalidation certification to MHI annually to continue eligibility
If OEM changes design or ex-factory price during the scheme tenure, fresh PM E-DRIVE eligibility certificate is required
If revalidation is not done within one month of expiry, registration under the scheme is liable to be cancelled
